name: Code Review Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday code review work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical code review tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday code review work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical code review tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep code review outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
2. Prefer the simplest code review approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Validate code review outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. Prefer explicit, readable code review solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Before starting code review work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Keep code review changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Document any non-obvious code review decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen code review approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of code review correctness.
- Do not skip documenting code review assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic code review advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop code review edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated code review concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these code review guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
